title: What If the Himalayan Glaciers Disappeared?

scenes.text: What if the Himalayan glaciers vanished? Nearly two billion people live downstream.
About 240 million people live in the mountains, and 1.65 billion more live along rivers that start there.
Rivers like the Ganges, Indus and Mekong are partly fed by glacier melt.
At first, melting makes rivers run higher. Flows are expected to peak around the middle of this century, then decline.
Glaciers there lost ice 65 percent faster in the 2010s than in the decade before.
Even if warming stays at 1.5 to 2 degrees, the region could lose a third to a half of its ice by 2100.
